exact_results: The existing literal spectatorScalingMap a b is the coercion of a complex continuous linear map on (Fin 3 + Fin d -> Complex).
Its action on the actual coordinate unit vector Pi.single i 1 is scalar multiplication by the corresponding block coefficient. Exact unit-direction norms are abs(a) for inl and abs(b) for inr.

For complex normed spaces, a continuous linear map g, and ContDiffAt of order n for f at the actual point g(x), the actual iterated derivative of f composed with g equals the iterated derivative of f composed in each direction with g.

On a coordinate word w : Fin n -> Fin 3 + Fin d, the actual iterated derivative after spectator scaling equals product_j(block coefficient at w_j) times the unscaled derivative on that same word at the scaled point.
The corresponding norm is bounded by the derivative operator norm at the scaled point times product_j norm(block coefficient at w_j), preserving separate spatial and spectator scale factors.
semantic_checks: The linear-map coercion is proved equal to the pre-existing scaling function, so no replacement map or coordinate interpretation is introduced.

The local chain rule uses only ContDiffAt at g(x). A smaller open neighborhood supplies the within-set theorem, then within derivatives agree with actual iterated derivatives. Global ContDiff is not assumed.
The coordinate vectors are actual Pi.single unit vectors and have norm one in the actual finite Pi norm.
No positivity, nonzero, invertibility or nondegeneracy hypotheses are imposed on a or b. Zero and negative scales are covered; norm conclusions use absolute values.
Derivative order zero uses the empty product one and zero-arity iterated derivative. Spectator dimension zero is included.
The product of directional factors is not replaced by max(abs(a),abs(b))^n.
